name: task
description: Complete task lifecycle: investigation with automated task/git/issue setup, implementation, code review, documentation, and user-verified completion.

steps.name: investigation
steps.description: Understand scope, clarify with user, define task file content for automated creation
steps.end:
Advance when:
- [ ] Task purpose, scope, and affected modules are fully understood — zero remaining questions.
- [ ] The user has EXPLICITLY agreed to the presented plan summary.
- [ ] Complete task file content composed following TEMPLATE.md, with measurable success criteria.
- [ ] Delivered WRITE-FILE-FIRST for substantial files: write team-management/tasks/<priority>-<name>.md (DIRECTORY task: <priority>-<name>/README.md), then advance with an empty task_content — args: {"task": "<priority>-<name>", "branch": "<type>/<name>", "task_content": ""} (small files may pass the full markdown inline). Keep the args object small and emit the call bare.
Note: with write-file-first, git_setup_branch (which runs first) pauses on the dirty tree — re-advance with carry_changes: true to carry the task file onto the new branch.

steps.name: implementation
steps.description: Implement the task, check off success criteria, pass all tests
steps.end:
Advance when:
- [ ] All success criteria in the task file are checked off.
- [ ] All new code is covered by tests and all tests pass.
- [ ] No unaddressed work remaining.
- [ ] Changes are NOT committed yet — the completion step handles git.

steps.name: code-review
steps.description: Spec compliance review + code quality review. Sentinel SPEC_REVIEW: PASSED required before advance. Summary must evidence verification. Optional test gate runs on advance-out when config.json defines test_command.
steps.end:
Advance when:
- [ ] Latest REVIEW_ROUND note matches the current tree — no code change after the final round.
- [ ] Code review passes with zero critical issues.
- [ ] Warnings: strict (enforce_warnings=true) → zero confirmed warnings (defects); relaxed (false or not set) → documented, non-blocking. Notes never block.
- [ ] Final passing review appended to the task work log in the exact format '# Code Review: [Title]' with Summary, Critical Issues, Warnings, and Notes sections.
- [ ] Advance summary includes verification evidence (fenced block, N/N passed, exit 0) or the 'no-verification-applicable: <reason>' escape hatch.
- [ ] Spec compliance audit passed on the final tree — SPEC_REVIEW: PASSED sentinel recorded after the last review round, followed by its SPEC_UNVERIFIABLE: and SPEC_DEFERRED: carriage notes.

steps.name: documentation
steps.description: Update CLAUDE.md files, finalize task work log, update wiki if enabled
steps.start:
Update documentation for all affected modules and systems.

SCOPE OF THIS STEP: Only documentation updates. If you discover code changes are needed, use protocol_goto(step_name="implementation") to return to implementation — do NOT write TODOs or skip code fixes.

CLAUDE.md files are a LEAN, LIVING REFERENCE OF THE CURRENT STATE — not a changelog. They are re-read into context every session, so every line costs tokens forever.
CONTENT TEST for every line: would a developer starting a new task tomorrow need this to find the code or avoid a mistake? If not, it does not belong.
- KEEP: module purpose; key files, one line each; non-obvious invariants and pitfalls; config keys.
- LEAVE OUT: review results and rounds; task names; versions something was verified on; history wording ("previously", "was removed", "renamed from", "no longer"); rationale narratives. Rationale goes to a wiki decision page, changes go to CHANGELOG.md, history lives in git and the task work log.
- REPLACE, DON'T APPEND: when this task changed behaviour, EDIT the existing description in place and DELETE the superseded wording.
- PRUNE as you go: remove obsolete, duplicated, or superseded entries you encounter.
- If a section has grown into a task-by-task narrative, consolidate it into a description of how the code works NOW.
- The check_claude_md_hygiene gate blocks advance when a line you ADDED names a task, uses history wording or carries review chatter, or when a CLAUDE.md grew past its line budget (documentation.claude_md_max_lines, default 300).

1. Run service-documentation agent with the list of all services/modules modified during implementation and the CURRENT behaviour of each — not the story of the task, its review rounds or its findings.
2. Run logging agent to finalize the task work log with completion summary and final status.
3. Verify all CLAUDE.md files for affected modules describe the CURRENT design accurately and concisely — editing in place and pruning superseded content, not appending a per-task delta.
4. Ensure the task work log has a complete chronological record of all work done. (The work log keeps full history — the conciseness rule above applies to CLAUDE.md, not the work log.)
5. Deferred documentation criteria. The spec audit at the end of code-review marks a documentation criterion it could not yet see done as DEFERRED and lists it in a SPEC_DEFERRED: carriage note. If the latest SPEC_DEFERRED: note lists SC-IDs, then after every documentation edit above (the check binds to the current tree, so a later edit makes it stale):
   a. Dispatch spec-compliance-reviewer in deferred-check mode: the task file path plus the listed SC-IDs.
   b. PASS (each listed item DONE or UNVERIFIABLE) → protocol_save_note("SPEC_DEFERRED: PASSED"). If any item came back UNVERIFIABLE, also save a fresh SPEC_UNVERIFIABLE: note listing the union with the earlier set, and append those items to the work-log carry-list (SC-ID + Verification Mode + why it is unverifiable + what the user should check).
   c. FAIL → write the missing documentation and re-dispatch. Never save SPEC_DEFERRED: PASSED without a PASS verdict.
   The require_deferred_criteria_done gate blocks advance until a SPEC_DEFERRED: PASSED note matches the current tree. If the code-review audit saved SPEC_DEFERRED: none, or no carriage at all, there is nothing to check. A SPEC_DEFERRED: list or none saved in this step does not count — only the step that ran the audit says what it deferred.

Note: documentation mode allows direct editing of CLAUDE.md files and task documentation but blocks source code edits. If a source code edit is blocked, use protocol_goto to go back to implementation.
steps.end:
Advance when:
- [ ] All CLAUDE.md files for affected modules describe the current design and pass the content test.
- [ ] check_claude_md_hygiene passes: no added line names a task, uses history wording or carries review chatter; no CLAUDE.md grew past its budget.
- [ ] Task work log is finalized with complete documentation of all work performed.
- [ ] require_deferred_criteria_done passes: every documentation criterion the spec audit deferred is confirmed by a SPEC_DEFERRED: PASSED note that matches the current tree.

steps.name: completion
steps.description: User tests changes, confirms, then dispatcher runs the provider-driven chain or the 4-option menu flow when issue tracking is disabled.
steps.end:
Advance when:
- [ ] User has tested the changes and explicitly confirmed everything works correctly.
On advance the engine automatically handles: committing and pushing changes, creating MR/PR (if provider enabled), updating issue status, archiving the task file, cleaning up task-scoped state, and clearing task state.
When issue_tracking.provider is 'disabled', the user picks a completion_option from the menu presented on step entry (merge_local / push_pr / keep / discard).
